item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate A is substantially closer to the frozen contract. It adds the exact required API and uses the established multipart helper, while B changes the signature, introduces forbidden association APIs, and expands multipart/options machinery unnecessarily.","reasons":["A defines the required signature exactly: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). B instead accepts ...UploadFileOption, violating the explicit API contract.","A directly reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content), as required. B adds and uses NewFileWithFields, duplicating and expanding established machinery.","B adds WithFileDealID, WithFilePersonID, other association options, and WithFileFormField despite the contract explicitly prohibiting association fields.","B changes the return types and implementation of WithFilesQuery and WithFilesRequestOptions and introduces several new option interfaces and configurations, creating avoidable API and maintenance complexity. A leaves FilesOption behavior intact and passes existing options through unchanged materially better than B does here, and both preserve the existing Add signature and implementation body."],"risks_a":["Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add, duplicating Add's request, decoding, and error logic in direct conflict with the contract.","It broadly changes RawClient retry and body-closing behavior for every seekable request body, despite the instruction not to refactor unrelated retry machinery.","The new Upload tests do not visibly cover propagation of a source-reader failure, which the contract explicitly requests."],"risks_b":["Upload has the wrong public signature and therefore fails the exact convenience-API requirement.","It adds explicitly forbidden association fields and arbitrary multipart form fields.","It uses NewFileWithFields and calls Raw.Do directly instead of reusing NewFile and routing through Add as required most clearly overall, making A the patch I would rather review and merge after requesting focused corrections." ]}
